institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The good reputation of Sciences Po with regards to the quality of the courses and Paris being an interesting and fun city that I did not know a lot about before.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very happy with the university, but not that happy with living at Cité Universitaire.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. Sciences Po are quite good at providing information, I would say.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Information sessions on zoom as well as several emails containing useful information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Sciences Po as an institution were good at providing information and answering emails quite quickly.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy. Cité Universitaire is an obvious choice.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Paris has quite good transport options, both metro and bikes (I rented a bike and used that throughout my semester). Therefore, it is not really a problem to live off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived at Cité Universitaire. I initially got a spot at the Danish House, but I was exchanged to the Spanish house. This was not the best experience, as the staff there did not speak any English, and neither did most of the other residents (most of them were Spanish).

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was relatively lucky with the courses I got, but a lot of other students were very unhappy because of the "first come, first served"-approach to allocating spots at courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The registration process opened for all exchange students at the same time, and it was just about being the fastest at clicking on the different courses. Very stressful, and not a very optimal was of doing it, but for me it ended well.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A zoom session as well as several comprehensive emails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful, I got all the classes I wanted - but many others did not and were very unsatisfied.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare for the course registration - make lists of your wishes, write down the codes for each course so you can find them quickly, and make "plan B's" so you don't end up having to sign up for completely irrelevant classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A very wide range of interesting courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was at the Paris Instititute of International Affairs (PSIA). The level was quite high and challenging, but I was very happy with that.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more empirical, I would say. Also, a lot of pre knowledge was assumed, which I sometimes found a bit difficult.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Security Issues in the Post-Soviet Periphery
The United States in the World
China as a Player in Global Governance
Europe and the Political Economy of Globalisation
The European Union and its Neighbours

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would probably recommend all of these five courses, as they were all interesting, well-structured and (apart from "EU and its neighbours") and on a high level.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I cannot come up with any.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing was perhaps a bit cheaper than I expected. Generally though, the prices were as I expected

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Many opportunities, but some of them were uneasily accessible for non-French speakers and/or exchange students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Various sports, book clubs, discussion clubs and political/activist groups.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The sports programmes are supposed to be good.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The Versailles Palace and the myriad of museums in Paris. Make sure to go to some of the other cities in France in the weekends as well (I went to Lille and Marseilles, can recommend both). Also, make sure to drink a lot of wine on all the Parisian cafés.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: This was a bit more difficult than I expected. My classmates were not as easily approachable as I had hoped, most of them were non-exchange students and already had many friends, and also there was often a language barrier.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly hung out with fellow Danish students, as I found it difficult to get local friends. Speaking better French would definitely have made this easier.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language (as mentioned).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The "café"- and going out culture. The fact that most people are very keen on going out and drinking wine. Very lovely.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Prepare a little bit of French at home, if you do not know anything (even a little bit of Duolingo will come in handy)
Because there are sooo many deadlines for presentations, written coursework etc., make sure to prepare a thorough time schedule for yourself so you do not crumble under stress at the end of the semester.
Be at peace with the fact that you might end up hanging out mostly with students from your own country - that is not necessarily just a bad thing.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: My stay was still affected a little bit by covid. Therefore, there will probably be better opportunities for socializing events in the future (fingers crossed).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Definitely the courses themselves. Very good and educational.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sometimes a sense of loneliness because of socializing being slightly more difficult than expected.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Overall, I can definitely recommend exchange at Sciences Po Paris.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
